XslashEntry.description: A parsed xslash entry: a JSON file describing where to download a prebuilt executable for each platform. The file may begin with a `#!` shebang line, which is stripped before the JSON is parsed.

final.description: If true, use this entry directly and skip project-level resolution.

name.description: Logical name; used as arg0 on exec and as the lookup key in `xslash.json`.

compose.description: Several artifacts composed into one directory, as an alternative to a single artifact. Mutually exclusive with the sibling artifact fields above.

digest.description: Expected digest of the downloaded artifact, in lowercase hex.

format.description: Archive/compression format, or omitted for a single raw file. One of `tar.gz`, `tar.xz`, `tar.zst`, `tar`, `gz`, `xz`, `zst`, `zip`.

hash.description: Hash algorithm used for `digest`; `blake3` is the only supported value.

path.description: Where this artifact goes inside the composed directory. For an archive format, the subpath it's extracted into (optional; defaults to the composed root). For a single-file format (`gz`/`xz`/`zst`/none), the path the single file is placed at; required.

providers.description: Sources to fetch this artifact from, tried in order.

type.description: Provider type, kept for dotslash compatibility.

url.description: The download URL. Must start with `http://` or `https://`.

size.description: Expected size of the downloaded artifact, in bytes.

strip.description: For an archive, strip this leading in-archive subpath: extract only the entries under it, rebasing them onto the destination (the composed root, or `path` when also set) with the prefix dropped; entries outside it are skipped. Omitted extracts the whole archive. Ignored for single-file formats. Lets archives that each wrap their payload in a differing leading directory merge into one tree (e.g. the Rust SDK's component tarballs onto a shared sysroot).

digest.description: Expected digest of the downloaded artifact, in lowercase hex. Required for a single-artifact platform; absent when `compose` is set.

format.description: Archive/compression format, or omitted for a single raw executable. One of `tar.gz`, `tar.xz`, `tar.zst`, `tar`, `gz`, `xz`, `zst`, `zip`.

hash.description: Hash algorithm used for `digest`; `blake3` is the only supported value. Required for a single-artifact platform; absent when `compose` is set.

path.description:
Where the executable is found within the extraction directory; it is run from `<extraction dir>/<path>`. Required.

- Archive formats: the path to the executable inside the extracted   archive.
- Single-file formats (`gz`/`xz`/`zst`/none): the path the decompressed   file — or, with no format, the raw binary — is placed at; that file   is itself the executable.
- With `compose` set: the path to the executable within the composed   directory.

providers.description: Sources to fetch the artifact from, tried in order. xslash only fetches `http`/`https` URLs; a provider with no `url` is skipped. Required for a single-artifact platform; absent when `compose` is set.

type.description: Provider type, kept for dotslash compatibility.

url.description: The download URL. Must start with `http://` or `https://`.

readonly.description: A dotslash-compatibility fallback for `rw`, which it should not co-exist with.

rw.description: If true, extract under `rw/` (mutable) instead of `ro/` (shared).

size.description: Expected size of the downloaded artifact, in bytes. Required for a single-artifact platform; absent when `compose` is set.

platforms.description:
Platform blocks keyed by `<kernel>-<arch>` — kernel one of `linux`, `darwin`, `windows`; arch one of `amd64`, `arm64` (e.g. `linux-amd64`). May be empty for a bare name-only entry that defers to project-level resolution.

Each block is either a single artifact (via `hash`/`digest`/`size`/ `providers`) or several composed into one directory (via `compose`); the two are mutually exclusive, and `path` is always required. These rules are enforced when the entry is resolved rather than by this type.
